checked_decisions.finding: Confirmed these three rows finish Isamu Alva Dyson (resource 2825010) before the speaker changes to Guld Goa Bowman at 16376 (resource 2825020), matching shout_groups.json. Targets ('That's nothing for me.', 'Done!', 'Home to drink!') match his reckless/carefree register.

(don't bunch up, spread out) compressed to 'Spread out!' under an 18-char budget, dropping the first half but keeping the command; 'Speed de kanau to omou na yo' (don't think speed alone will beat me) rendered as the declarative 'Speed alone won't win.' -- same warning-to-opponent content, no reversal.

Extreme edge case: source 'Tsugi!' (2 visible chars including the exclamation mark) gives a hard 2-character budget by the stated formula. No English rendering of 'next [target]' fits 2 characters; 'Go' is as close as any 2-char string gets and does not invert or misattribute meaning. This is a fit constraint, not a translator error -- kept as meaning_reviewed rather than draft, since the meaning has been checked as far as the format allows.

'Mattaku kisama to iu yatsu wa......' (roughly 'honestly, what a guy you are...', an exasperated address, likely to an ally) is rendered as 'Honestly, what a fool...'. The added evaluative word 'fool' is not literally in the source, but the underlying exasperated/scolding register is present in the source's context (kisama is a rough, contemptuous 'you') and fits Guld's disciplined, short-tempered characterization. Ruled acceptable as an idiomatic rendering of the exasperation rather than an invented judgment, but flagged below since it is a closer call than the rest of this batch.

'Sono choushi da' (keep that up / that's the way) rendered as 'Just so.' -- unusual phrasing in modern English but not incorrect, and its clipped formality suits Guld's terse commanding voice; left as is per 'fix what is wrong, leave what is merely different'.
